title: I Am With You Always
subtitle: Matthew in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Matthew begins with a long list of names, four surprising mothers tucked inside it, and ends on a mountain with a promise: I am with you always. In between: a star over a small house, a family slipping away by night, fishing nets left on the shore, salt and a lamp on a stand, birds that never plant and wildflowers that never spin, a house that stands in the storm, a mustard seed, a pearl, a hand reaching down to a sinking man, and a stone rolled away at dawn.

This book walks through it in forty short poems, in five parts that follow Matthew's own rhythm of story and teaching. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the story touches—a loaf and a stone, a yoke on a wall, a lamp gone out in a garden—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the Gospel of Matthew alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: God With Us
parts.epigraph: She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.
parts.lightHint: Near 'the names' (Matthew 1:3–6) in Part 1: God With Us
parts.zh_epigraph: 她将生下一个儿子。你要给他起名叫耶稣，因为他要把他的子民从罪恶中拯救出来。

parts.title: Blessed
parts.epigraph: Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven.
parts.lightHint: Near 'poor in spirit' (Matthew 5:1–3) in Part 2: Blessed
parts.zh_epigraph: 你们要欢喜快乐，因为你们在天上的赏赐是大的。

parts.title: Come to Me
parts.epigraph: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
parts.lightHint: Near 'I want to' (Matthew 8:1–3) in Part 3: Come to Me
parts.zh_epigraph: 凡劳苦担重担的人，可以到我这里来，我就使你们得安息。

parts.title: On This Rock
parts.epigraph: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
parts.lightHint: Near 'crumbs' (Matthew 15:21–28) in Part 4: On This Rock
parts.zh_epigraph: 你是基督，永生神的儿子。

parts.title: Watch with Me
parts.epigraph: Stay here, and watch with me.
parts.lightHint: Near 'humble, on a donkey' (Matthew 21:1–11) in Part 5: Watch with Me
parts.zh_epigraph: 留在这儿，和我一起观看。

paintings.title: the names
paintings.epigraph: “Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth.”
paintings.poem:
a long list of fathers.
the kind of page
you skim.

and then, four times,
a mother slips in:

Tamar, who was wronged.
Rahab, from the house on Jericho's wall.
Ruth, the foreigner.
Uriah's wife,
not even named.

every one of them
a story
someone might have left out.

they were written in.

the family of Jesus
has room
for a story like yours.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the stones of the wall: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “the family of Jesus has room for a story like yours”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一长串父亲的名单。
页面类型
你略读。

然后，四次，
一位母亲溜了进来：

塔玛，受了委屈。
喇合，来自耶利哥城墙上的房子。
露丝，外国人。
乌利亚的妻子，
甚至没有命名。

他们每一个人
一个故事
有人可能被遗漏了。

它们被写在。

耶稣的家人
有房间
对于像你这样的故事。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在墙上石头周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“耶稣的家庭有空间容纳像你这样的故事”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静的祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “波阿斯与路得生了俄备得。”

paintings.title: a quiet man
paintings.epigraph: “Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example”
paintings.poem:
he had every right
to make a scene.
he didn't.

even hurt,
he chose the quiet way,
the one that would cost her least.

and while he was still turning it over,
God spoke to him in his sleep:
don't be afraid.

so he got up and did it.

Matthew never gives him
a single line to say.
he didn't need one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “a quiet man” (Matthew 1:19–24) from “he had every right to make a scene” to “Matthew never gives him a single line to say. he didn't need one”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
他有一切权利
制造一个场景。
他没有。

甚至受伤，
他选择了安静的方式，
对她来说花费最少的一个。

当他还在翻动它的时候，
神在他睡梦中对他说话：
别害怕。

于是他就站起来做了。

马修从来不给他
一句话说。
他不需要一个。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留心“一个安静的人”（马太福音 1：19-24）中的情节，从“他完全有权大吵大闹”到“马太从来没有给他一句话可说。他不需要任何一句话”——今天你发现自己处于这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她的丈夫约瑟夫是一个正义的人，不愿意让她成为公众的榜样”

paintings.title: God with us
paintings.epigraph: “They shall call his name Immanuel;” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.””
paintings.poem:
not God above us.
not God against us.
not God
somewhere far off,
waiting to be found.

God
with
us.

the whole good news
fits in three words.

hold on to them.
this book
will end
the same way.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “God with us” (Matthew 1:23) arrives at: “this book will end the same way.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
不是高于我们的上帝。
不是上帝反对我们。
不是上帝
某个遥远的地方，
等待被发现。

上帝
与
我们。

整个好消息
适合三个字。

抓住他们。
这本书
将结束
同样的方式。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“神与我们同在”（马太福音 1：23）如何得出：“这本书也会以同样的方式结束。”你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们要给他起名叫以马内利；”被解释为“上帝与我们同在”。

paintings.title: the star
paintings.epigraph: “When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.”
paintings.poem:
they came from the east,
reading the sky.
strangers.
outsiders to the promise.

they asked at the palace.
the king was troubled.
the scholars knew the verse
by heart.

the strangers
were the ones who went.

and the star moved again
and stood still
over one small house.

exceedingly great joy.

sometimes the ones
who travel farthest
are the first
to kneel.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Matthew 2:1–10: “sometimes the ones who travel farthest are the first to kneel”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他们来自东方，
阅读天空。
陌生人。
外人来许诺。

他们在宫殿里问道。
国王很烦恼。
学者们知道这节经文
凭心而论。

陌生人
是那些去了的人。

星星又移动了
并站着不动
超过一栋小房子。

非常大的喜悦。

有时那些
谁旅行最远
是第一个
跪下。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是马太福音 2 章 1-10 节的安静教训：“有时走得最远的人是第一个跪下的”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “当他们看到那颗星时，他们非常高兴。”

paintings.title: treasures
paintings.epigraph: “Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.”
paintings.poem:
gold for a king.
frankincense for worship.
myrrh for a burial.

that's how the church
has long read them.

strange things
to bring a child.

as if the whole story
was already there
in their hands:
who he was,
why he came,
what it would cost.

they fell down,
and then
they opened what they had.

that is still
the way to come.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside your own two hands: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “that is still the way to come”?
paintings.zh_poem:
国王的黄金。
供奉乳香。
没药用于埋葬。

教会就是这样
已经读了很久了。

奇怪的事情
带孩子。

仿佛整个故事
已经在那里了
在他们手中：
他是谁，
他为什么来，
会花费多少钱。

他们跌倒了，
然后
他们打开了他们所拥有的东西。

那仍然是
未来的路。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下站在这个框架内，旁边是你自己的两只手：当你听到“这仍然是未来的方式”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们打开宝藏，向他献上礼物：黄金、乳香和没药。”

paintings.title: another way
paintings.epigraph: “they went back to their own country another way.”
paintings.poem:
you don't go home
the way you came
once you've knelt
in front of him.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “you don't go home the way you came once you've knelt in front of him.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Matthew 2:12 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
你不回家
你来的路
一旦你跪下
在他面前。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“一旦你跪在他面前，你就不会再按来时的路回家了。”马太福音 2 章 12 节现在最能触动你内心的哪个部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们以另一种方式回到了自己的国家。”

paintings.title: by night
paintings.epigraph: “He arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt”
paintings.poem:
no time to pack the house.
no time to say goodbye.

just a dream,
a warning,
and a man getting up
in the dark.

the Son of God
was carried across a border
in the middle of the night.

if you've ever had to leave
everything behind,
he knows that road.

and he knows the God
who says,
stay there
until I tell you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Matthew 2:13–15, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “by night”: how does the closing thought—“and he knows the God who says, stay there until I tell you”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
没有时间收拾房子。
没有时间说再见。

只是一个梦，
警告，
和一个男人站起来
在黑暗中。

神的儿子
被带过边境
半夜。

如果你曾经不得不离开
一切的背后，
他认识那条路。

他认识上帝
谁说，
留在那里
直到我告诉你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在马太福音 2 章 13-15 节中，恩典就在“夜间”安静的核心内容旁边与我们相遇：结尾的思想——“他认识那位说，你留在那里，直到我告诉你”——如何为你在前面的道路上站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “夜间，他起身，带着小孩子和他母亲，往埃及去”

paintings.title: the heavens opened
paintings.epigraph: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
paintings.poem:
John tried to stop him.
I need to be baptized by you.

but he waded in anyway,
into the same river
as everyone
who had come to confess.

and when he came up
out of the water,
the sky opened,
a dove came down,
and a voice said
beloved.

he hadn't preached yet.
hadn't healed anyone.
hadn't done
a single miracle.

the Father
was already pleased.22
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “the heavens opened” (Matthew 3:13–17) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“the Father was already pleased.22”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
约翰试图阻止他。
我需要接受你的洗礼。

但他还是涉水而入，
流入同一条河
和大家一样
谁来告白了。

当他上来的时候
从水里出来，
天开了，
一只鸽子落下来，
一个声音说
亲爱的。

他还没有讲道。
没有治愈任何人。
没有做
一个奇迹。

父亲
已经很高兴了。22
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁边挂着今天的“天开了”（马太福音 3：13-17）的画，那么它的最后一行——“父已经喜悦了。22”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这是我的爱子，我对他感到非常满意。”

paintings.title: nets
paintings.epigraph: “They immediately left their nets and followed him.”
paintings.poem:
two brothers casting.
two more mending.

ordinary work
on an ordinary morning.

come after me.

and they left the nets
where they lay,
and the boat,
and their father
still sitting in it.

he didn't hand them
a plan.
he handed them
himself.

the rest
they would learn
on the road.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Matthew 4:18–22)—where in your own home or work today does “the rest they would learn on the road” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
两兄弟选角。
还有两个正在修补。

普通工作
在一个平凡的早晨。

来追我吧。

他们离开了网
他们躺着的地方，
和船，
和他们的父亲
还坐在里面。

他没有递给他们
一个计划。
他递给他们
他自己。

其余的
他们会学习
在路上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平凡的地方与我们相遇（马太福音 4：18-22）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作中，“他们在路上学到的其他知识”听起来是否属实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们立即丢下网，跟着他。”

paintings.title: poor in spirit
paintings.epigraph: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.”
paintings.poem:
he sat down on a hillside,
and the first word
out of his mouth
was blessed.

not to the ones
who had it together.

to the poor in spirit.
the ones with nothing left
to bring
but their need.

that's where
the kingdom starts:

empty hands,
open.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “that's where the kingdom starts: empty hands, open.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
他坐在山坡上，
和第一个词
从他嘴里出来
受到祝福。

不给那些
谁在一起了。

给精神上贫穷的人。
那些一无所有的人
带来
但他们的需要。

那就是那里
王国开始：

双手空空，
打开。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 慢慢吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“这就是王国开始的地方：双手空空，张开。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “精神贫穷的人有福了，因为天国是他们的。”

paintings.title: those who mourn
paintings.epigraph: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.”
paintings.poem:
blessed
is not the word
you expect
at a graveside.

but he said it
to the grieving:

you shall be comforted.

not cheer up.
not it wasn't that bad.

comforted.
a promise
with arms.

some blessings
arrive
with the tears
still on them.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “blessed is not the word you expect at a graveside.” Looking through the lens of Matthew 5:4, what does it mean to discover that “some blessings arrive with the tears still on them”?
paintings.zh_poem:
有福的
不是这个词
你期望
在坟墓边。

但他说了
致悲伤：

你会得到安慰。

不高兴。
不，没那么糟糕。

安慰了。
一个承诺
带武器。

一些祝福
到达
带着泪水
仍然在他们身上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下某个季节，当您知道“在墓地边所期望的词不是祝福”的感觉时。透过马太福音 5 章 4 节的镜头，我们会发现“有些福气临到时，还带着眼泪”是什么意思？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “哀恸的人有福了，因为他们必得到安慰。”

paintings.title: salt
paintings.epigraph: “You are the salt of the earth”
paintings.poem:
salt doesn't ask
to be noticed.

a pinch
disappears into the bread,
the fish,
the pot of lentils,
and everything
tastes more like itself.

it keeps things
from spoiling, too.

you are the salt
of the earth,
he told fishermen
and farmers
on a hill.

a little of you
can change the taste
of a whole room.32
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the daily loaf broken in the hand in this painting (Matthew 5:13)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
盐不问
被注意到。

一点
消失在面包里，
鱼，
扁豆锅，
和一切
味道更像它本身。

它保留东西
也免于变质。

你是盐
地球的，
他告诉渔民
和农民
在一座小山上。

你的一点点
可以改变味道
整个房间的32
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中每天手中擘开的面包（马太福音 5:13）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你是地球之盐”

paintings.title: on a stand
paintings.epigraph: “Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.”
paintings.poem:
nobody lights a lamp
and hides it
under a basket.

that would be
a strange kind of modesty.

you set it up high
where it can reach the corners.

and nobody praises
the lamp.
they just find their way
across the room.

let it shine like that,
so they look up
and thank your Father.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the small oil lamp in the dark: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “let it shine like that, so they look up and thank your Father”?
paintings.zh_poem:
没有人点灯
并隐藏它
在一个篮子下。

那将是
一种奇怪的谦虚。

你把它设置得很高
它可以到达角落的地方。

并且没有人赞扬
灯。
他们只是找到自己的路
穿过房间。

就让它这样闪耀吧
所以他们抬头看
感谢你的父亲。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的眼睛在黑暗中停留在小油灯周围的笔触和灯光上：当你读到“让它如此发光，以便他们抬头感谢你的父亲”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “点灯也不放在斗底下，而是放在灯台上，灯就照亮家里的所有人。”

paintings.title: sun and rain
paintings.epigraph: “he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.”
paintings.poem:
the sun comes up
on both sides of the wall.
the rain doesn't check
whose field it's falling on.

that's what your Father is like,
he said. so be like that.

love your enemy.
pray for the one who hurt you.

it will feel like too much.
the sun has never once
asked who deserved it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “sun and rain” (Matthew 5:43–45) from “the sun comes up on both sides of the wall” to “the sun has never once asked who deserved it”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
太阳升起
在墙壁的两侧。
雨不检查
它落在谁的领域。

你的父亲就是这样的人
他说。所以就这样吧。

爱你的敌人。
为伤害你的人祈祷。

会感觉太多了。
太阳从来没有一次
问谁罪有应得。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 徘徊在“阳光和雨水”（马太福音 5：43-45）的乐章中，从“太阳从墙的两边升起”到“太阳从来没有问过谁应得的”——今天你发现自己在这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他使日头照耀恶人，也照善人；降雨给义人，也给不义的人。”

paintings.title: the inner room
paintings.epigraph: “your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.”
paintings.poem:
go into the small room.
shut the door.

no audience.
no one to impress.
no need for
the right words,
or a lot of them.

he already knows
what you need.

so why pray?

because it was never
about informing him.

your Father
is in secret, he said.

shut the door.
he's already
on your side of it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “the inner room” (Matthew 6:6–8) arrives at: “he's already on your side of it.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
走进小房间。
关上门。

没有观众。
没有人留下深刻印象。
不需要
正确的话，
或者很多。

他已经知道了
你需要什么。

那么为什么要祈祷呢？

因为从来没有
关于通知他。

你的父亲
他说，这是秘密的。

关上门。
他已经
在你这边。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“内室”（马太福音 6：6-8）是如何出现的：“他已经在你这边了。”你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在你祈求之前，你的天父就知道你需要什么。”

paintings.title: tomorrow
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself.”
paintings.poem:
the birds on the roof
didn't plant a thing.
they're fed.

the wildflowers on the hill
never sewed a stitch.
Solomon never looked
so fine.

and the grass,
green today,
kindling tomorrow,
still gets dressed
by God.

so leave tomorrow
where it is.
it can worry
about itself.

today has enough in it
without borrowing
from the next one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Matthew 6:26–34: “today has enough in it without borrowing from the next one”?
paintings.zh_poem:
屋顶上的鸟儿
没有种东西。
他们吃饱了。

山上的野花
从来没有缝过一针。
所罗门从未看过
很好。

还有草，
今天绿色，
点燃明天，
仍然穿好衣服
由上帝。

所以明天离开
它在哪里。
它会担心
关于它自己。

今天已经足够了
无需借钱
从下一张开始。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是马太福音 6 章 26-34 节的安静教训：“今天已经够了，不需要向下借借”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “所以不要为明天焦虑，因为明天会为自己焦虑。”

paintings.title: bread, not a stone
paintings.epigraph: “Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?”
paintings.poem:
ask. seek. knock.

and in case you wonder
who is on the other side of the door,
he tells you: a father.

no father hands
his hungry child a stone.

and you, who get so much wrong,
still know how to give good gifts.

how much more
your Father in heaven.
so ask.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the daily loaf broken in the hand: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “how much more your Father in heaven. so ask”?
paintings.zh_poem:
问。寻找。敲。

如果你想知道
谁在门的另一边
他告诉你：一个父亲。

没有父亲的手
他饥饿的孩子是一块石头。

而你，犯了这么多错误，
还是知道如何送好礼物。

还有多少
你在天上的父。
所以问。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在这个框架内，旁边是每天手中破碎的面包：当你听到“更何况你的天父。所以问”时，你一周中的匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “或者你们中间有谁，如果他的儿子向他要面包，会给他一块石头呢？”

paintings.title: the same storm
paintings.epigraph: “The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall”
paintings.poem:
both houses
got the same storm.

same rain.
same rising water.
same wind
leaning on the walls.

the difference
wasn't the weather.

it was what lay underneath,
down where nobody looks
while the sun is out.

hearing isn't building.
doing is.

dig down
while the sky is clear.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “dig down while the sky is clear.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Matthew 7:24–27 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
两栋房子
遭遇了同样的风暴。

同样的雨。
同样上涨的水。
同样的风
靠在墙上。

区别
不是天气。

就是下面的东西，
在没人看的地方
当太阳出来的时候。

听力没有建立。
正在做的是。

向下挖掘
天空晴朗。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“趁天空晴朗，向下挖掘。”马太福音 7 章 24-27 节现在最能触动你内心的哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “雨淋了，水冲了，风吹了，撞着那房子，它却没有倒塌。”

paintings.title: I want to
paintings.epigraph: “Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.””
paintings.poem:
if you want to,
you can.

he never doubted
the power.
he wasn't sure
about the want.

no one had touched him
in how long?

and Jesus
reached out his hand
and touched him
as he said it:

I want to.

he still does.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Matthew 8:1–3, grace meets us right beside your own two hands: how does the closing thought—“and Jesus reached out his hand and touched him as he said it: I want to. he still does”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
如果你愿意的话
你可以。

他从不怀疑
的力量。
他不确定
关于想要的。

没有人碰过他
多长时间？

和耶稣
伸出手
并触碰了他
正如他所说：

我想要。

他仍然这样做。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在马太福音 8 章 1-3 节中，恩典就在你的两只手旁边与我们相遇：最后的思想——“耶稣伸手摸他，说：我愿意。他仍然愿意”——如何为你前面的路站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: ”耶稣伸出手来摸他，说：“我愿意。变得干净起来。””

paintings.title: follow me
paintings.epigraph: “he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office.”
paintings.poem:
this gospel carries his name.
a tax collector,
the kind people crossed the street to avoid.

two words: follow me.
and he got up and left the table.

that night his house was full
of people like him,
eating with Jesus.

the healthy, Jesus said,
don't need a doctor.
he goes where the sick are.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “follow me” (Matthew 9:9–13) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“he goes where the sick are”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
这本福音书以他的名字命名。
税吏，
善良的人们过马路要避开。

两个字：跟我来。
他起身离开了桌子。

那天晚上他的房子挤满了人
像他这样的人，
与耶稣一起吃饭。

耶稣说，健康的人，
不需要医生。
有病人的地方他就去。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的画作“跟从我”（马太福音 9：9-13），那么它的最后一句“他往病人所在的地方去”会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他看到一个叫马修的人坐在税收办公室里。”

paintings.title: a cup of cold water
paintings.epigraph: “Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink”
paintings.poem:
not a fortune.
not a sermon.
just a cup of cold water,
and heaven never forgets it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Matthew 10:42)—where in your own home or work today does “just a cup of cold water, and heaven never forgets it” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
不是一笔财富。
不是布道。
只需要一杯凉水，
天堂永远不会忘记它。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平凡的地方与我们相遇（马太福音 10:42）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作场所，“一杯凉水，天必不忘”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “谁给这些小孩子一杯凉水喝”

paintings.title: an easy yoke
paintings.epigraph: “For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
paintings.poem:
a yoke is not a way out of work.
it's a way to share the load:
one beam, two shoulders, one pace.

come to me,
all you who are tired,
all you carrying too much.

he doesn't say
drop everything and walk away.
he says walk with me.
I am gentle, humble in heart.

and somehow, step by step,
the load gets light.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “and somehow, step by step, the load gets light.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
枷锁并不是摆脱工作的出路。
这是一种分担负载的方式：
一梁，两肩，一步。

到我这里来，
所有疲惫的你们
你们都背负了太多。

他没有说
放下一切走开。
他说和我一起走。
我性格温柔，内心谦虚。

不知何故，一步一步，
负载变轻。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 慢慢吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“不知怎的，一步一步，负担变轻了。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为我的轭是容易的，我的担子是轻省的。”

paintings.title: a bruised reed
paintings.epigraph: “He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a smoking flax”
paintings.poem:
a reed bent
nearly in half.
a wick
that's more smoke
than flame.

most of us
would snap the one,
pinch out the other,
and start over.

not him.

he doesn't shout.
he doesn't hurry.

he cups his hand
around what's left
until it catches.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “a reed bent nearly in half.” Looking through the lens of Matthew 12:18–21, what does it mean to discover that “he cups his hand around what's left until it catches”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一根芦苇弯曲
几乎一半。
一根灯芯
那是更多的烟
比火焰。

我们大多数人
会折断那个，
捏掉另一个，
并重新开始。

不是他。

他没有喊叫。
他不着急。

他把手捧成杯状
围绕剩下的
直到它抓住。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下你体验过“芦苇几乎弯成两半”的感觉的一个季节。从马太福音 12 章 18-21 节的角度看，发现“他用手捧着剩下的东西，直到它接住”，这意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他不会折断压伤的芦苇。他不会吹灭将残的灯火”

paintings.title: the smallest seed
paintings.epigraph: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed”
paintings.poem:
you could lose it
in a crease
of your palm.

you'd never guess,
looking at it,
that birds would one day
rest in its branches.

that's how the kingdom
looks at the start:
too small to notice.

whatever he's planted in you
may still look
like nothing much.

give it time.

there are birds
coming.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the small seed hidden in the soil in this painting (Matthew 13:31–32)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
你可能会失去它
在折痕中
你的手掌。

你绝对想不到，
看着它，
有一天，鸟儿会
安息在它的枝条上。

王国就是这样
看开头：
太小了，无法注意到。

无论他在你身上种下了什么
可能仍然看起来
没什么特别喜欢的。

给它时间。

有鸟
来了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中隐藏在土壤中的小种子（马太福音13:31-32）——如果你今天可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “天国就像一粒芥菜种”

paintings.title: one pearl
paintings.epigraph: “who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.”
paintings.poem:
a man finds treasure
hidden in a field,
and sells everything.

a merchant finds
one pearl,
and sells everything.

from the outside
it looks like loss.

from the inside
it's the best trade
anyone ever made.

look for the word
Jesus tucked in:

in his joy.

nobody
had to make him.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the quiet centerpiece of “one pearl”: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “from the inside it's the best trade anyone ever made. nobody had to make him”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一个人发现了宝藏
隐藏在田野里，
并出售一切。

一个商人发现
一颗珍珠，
并出售一切。

从外面
看起来像是损失。

从里面
这是最好的交易
任何人曾经做过。

寻找这个词
耶稣塞进：

在他的喜悦中。

没有人
不得不让他。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让您的目光停留在“一颗珍珠”安静中心周围的笔触和光线上：当您读到“从内部来看，这是任何人做过的最好的交易。没有人必须做他”时，您内心会升起什么样的安静祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他遇见一颗重价的珍珠，就去变卖他一切所有的，买了这颗珍珠。”

paintings.title: come
paintings.epigraph: “Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him”
paintings.poem:
the fourth watch of the night.
the wind against them.
a shape on the water.

Lord, if it's you,
tell me to come.
come.

for a few steps Peter walked
on what can't be walked on.
then he looked at the wind
and began to go under.

three words were all the prayer he had:
Lord, save me.

it was enough.
immediately, a hand.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “come” (Matthew 14:24–33) from “the fourth watch of the night” to “it was enough. immediately, a hand”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
夜四更。
迎着他们的风。
水面上的一个形状。

主啊，如果是你，
告诉我来。
来。

彼得走了几步
在不能行走的地方。
然后他看着风
并开始下跌。

他的祈祷只有三个字：
主啊，救救我吧。

这就足够了。
立刻，一只手。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留心“来”（马太福音 14：24-33）中从“四更”到“够了。立刻伸出手来”——今天你发现自己处于这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶稣立刻伸手拉住他”

paintings.title: crumbs
paintings.epigraph: “Y es, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”
paintings.poem:
a foreign woman calling after them,
a daughter at home in torment.

he answered her not a word.
the disciples said, send her away.

she didn't go away.
she knelt and said, Lord, help me.

and when the answer still sounded like no,
she argued with the Son of God
using crumbs.

woman, great is your faith.

sometimes faith looks a lot like
refusing to leave.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “crumbs” (Matthew 15:21–28) arrives at: “sometimes faith looks a lot like refusing to leave.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
一个外国女人在后面呼唤他们，
女儿在家受尽折磨。

他没有回答她一句话。
门徒说，打发她走吧。

她没有走开。
她跪下说，主啊，帮助我。

当答案听起来仍然是“不”时，
她与上帝的儿子争论
使用面包屑。

女人，你的信仰是伟大的。

有时信仰看起来很像
拒绝离开。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“碎屑”（马太福音 15：21-28）是如何产生的：“有时信心看起来很像拒绝离开。”你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “是的，主啊，但是连狗也吃主人桌子上掉下来的面包屑。”

paintings.title: who do you say
paintings.epigraph: “But who do you say that I am?”
paintings.poem:
some said John. some said Elijah,
or Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.

then the question turned around:
but who do you say?

Simon said it straight:
the Christ, the Son of the living God.

and Jesus called him Peter, the rock,
and promised a church
the gates of Hades would not outlast.

a few verses later he'd get it wrong.
the answer still stood.

nobody else
can answer it for you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Matthew 16:13–18: “nobody else can answer it for you”?
paintings.zh_poem:
有人说约翰。有人说以利亚，
或耶利米，或一位先知。

然后问题就转过来了：
但你说谁呢？

西蒙直接说道：
基督，永生神的儿子。

耶稣称他为磐石彼得，
并承诺建造一座教堂
哈迪斯之门不会长久。

几节之后他就听错了。
答案仍然成立。

没有其他人
可以为您解答。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是马太福音 16 章 13-18 节中安静的教训：“没有人能为你解答”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但是你说我是谁？”

paintings.title: get up
paintings.epigraph: “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”
paintings.poem:
a face shining like the sun.
Moses and Elijah.
a bright cloud,
a voice:
listen to him.

and three fishermen
face down on the ground,
terrified.

then a touch.
get up.
don't be afraid.

when they lifted their eyes,
the brightness was gone.
the visitors were gone.

only Jesus.

it was
enough.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the guiding cloud: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “only Jesus. it was enough”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一张像太阳一样闪闪发光的脸。
摩西和以利亚。
一朵明亮的云，
一个声音：
听他说。

和三个渔民
面朝下趴在地上，
害怕。

然后触摸。
起床。
别害怕。

当他们抬起眼睛的时候
亮度消失了。
访客都走了。

只有耶稣。

原来是
够了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在这个框架内，在引导云的旁边：当你听到“只有耶稣。这就足够了”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “起来吧，别害怕。”

paintings.title: in the middle
paintings.epigraph: “Jesus called a little child to himself, and set him in the middle of them”
paintings.poem:
they wanted to know
who would be the greatest.

so he called a child over
and set him
right in the middle
of the argument.

no title.
no track record.
nothing to prove.

just someone
small enough
to come
when he's called.

turn, he said,
and become like this.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “turn, he said, and become like this.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Matthew 18:1–4 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
他们想知道
谁将是最伟大的。

于是他叫了一个孩子过来
并设置他
就在中间
的论点。

没有标题。
没有跟踪记录。
没有什么可以证明的。

只是某人
足够小
来
当他被召唤时。

转过来，他说，
并变成这样。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声读出结束语：“转动，他说，变成这样。”马太福音 18 章 1-4 节现在最能触动你内心的哪个部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶稣叫了一个小孩子来，把他放在他们中间”

paintings.title: seventy times seven
paintings.epigraph: “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.”
paintings.poem:
seven times
must have sounded generous.

seventy times seven.
he didn't mean keep count longer.
he meant put the count away.

then he told of a servant
let off a debt too big to ever repay,
who walked straight out
and seized a friend over a smaller one.

once you see how much
you've been let go of,
every debt owed to you
looks different.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Matthew 18:21–35, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “seventy times seven”: how does the closing thought—“once you see how much you've been let go of, every debt owed to you looks different”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
七次
听起来一定很慷慨。

七十乘七。
他的意思并不是要再数下去。
他的意思是把计数收起来。

然后他谈到了一个仆人
免除一笔太大而无法偿还的债务，
谁径直走了出来
并抓住了一个朋友而不是一个较小的朋友。

一旦你看到多少
你已经被释放了
欠你的每一笔债
看起来不一样。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在马太福音 18 章 21-35 节中，恩典就在“七十个七”的安静核心旁边与我们相遇：最后的思想——“一旦你看到自己被释放了多少，欠你的每一笔债看起来都不同了”——如何为你在前面的道路上站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我直到七次才告诉你，但是，直到七十个七次。”

paintings.title: the eleventh hour
paintings.epigraph: “Because no one has hired us.”
paintings.poem:
late afternoon.
the marketplace nearly empty.
a few still standing there,
the ones nobody picked all day.

why are you idle?
because no one hired us.
and the owner said, you too. go.

at evening he paid them first,
and paid them a full day.
the ones who'd worked since dawn grumbled.

he wasn't cheating anyone.
he was just good.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “the eleventh hour” (Matthew 20:1–15) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“he wasn't cheating anyone. he was just good”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
下午晚些时候。
市场几乎空无一人。
有几个还站在那里
整天没人挑选的。

你为什么闲着？
因为没有人雇用我们。
店主说，你也是。去。

晚上他先付钱给他们，
并付给他们一整天的工资。
那些从黎明就开始工作的人抱怨道。

他没有欺骗任何人。
他很好。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“第十一小时”（马太福音 20:1-15）的画，那么它的最后一行——“他没有欺骗任何人。他只是很好”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为没有人雇用我们。”

paintings.title: humble, on a donkey
paintings.epigraph: “behold, your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey”
paintings.poem:
kings rode in
on warhorses,
with soldiers,
with noise.

this one
borrowed a donkey.

the crowd threw their cloaks
on the road,
cut branches from the trees,
and shouted hosanna.

the whole city asked,
who is this?

a king
close enough to touch,

riding low,
at the speed
of a walk.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Matthew 21:1–11)—where in your own home or work today does “a king close enough to touch, riding low, at the speed of a walk” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
国王骑马进来
战马之上，
与士兵，
有噪音。

这个
借了一头驴。

人群扔下了他们的斗篷
在路上，
从树上砍下树枝，
并高呼和散那。

全城人都问，
这是谁？

一个国王
足够近，可以触摸，

低位骑行，
以速度
散步的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平凡的地方与我们相遇（马太福音 21:1-11）——今天，在你自己的家中或工作场所，“一位君王近在咫尺，骑在低处，以步行的速度”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “看哪，你的国王骑着驴，谦卑地来到你身边”

paintings.title: as a hen
paintings.epigraph: “How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!”
paintings.poem:
after all the hard words,
this.

not a lion.
not an eagle.
a hen,
wings spread,
calling the little ones in
before the storm.

how often
I would have.

you would not.

God does not
drag anyone
under his wings.

but the wings
are still open.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “but the wings are still open.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
在说了这么多难听的话之后
这个。

不是狮子。
不是鹰。
一只母鸡，
翅膀展开，
叫小孩子进来
暴风雨来临之前。

多久一次
我会的。

你不会。

神不
拖任何人
在他的羽翼下。

但翅膀
仍然开放。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 慢慢吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“但翅膀仍然张开。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我多少次会把你的孩子们聚集在一起，就像母鸡把小鸡聚集在翅膀下一样，而你却不会！”

paintings.title: well done
paintings.epigraph: “Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things.”
paintings.poem:
five, two, one.
each according to his ability.
nobody was asked to match anyone else.

two went and traded
and doubled what they had.
one was afraid,
and buried his in the ground.

fear never grew anything.

well done.
faithful over a few things.
that was all he asked.

and then the best part:
enter into the joy.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “five, two, one. each according to his ability.” Looking through the lens of Matthew 25:14–23, what does it mean to discover that “and then the best part: enter into the joy”?
paintings.zh_poem:
五，二，一。
各尽所能。
没有人被要求与其他人匹配。

两个人去交易
并将他们所拥有的加倍。
一个人害怕，
并将他的埋在地下。

恐惧永远不会产生任何东西。

干得好。
在一些事情上忠诚。
他只问了这些。

然后是最好的部分：
进入喜悦之中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下一个赛季，当你体验到“五、二、一。各尽其能”的感觉时。从马太福音 25 章 14-23 节的角度来看，发现“然后是最好的部分：进入喜乐”意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “干得好，善良而忠诚的仆人。你在一些事情上一直忠心，我会让你做很多事情。”

paintings.title: the least of these
paintings.epigraph: “because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.”
paintings.poem:
when did we see you?

they honestly
didn't know.

they had only seen
a hungry man,
a thirsty woman,
a stranger at the door,
someone with no coat,
someone sick,
someone locked away.

they gave bread.
they gave a cup.
they gave a coat.
they sat a while.

and he was there
the whole time,

in whoever
needed them.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the torn and mended coat in this painting (Matthew 25:35–40)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们什么时候见过你？

他们诚实地
不知道。

他们只看到了
一个饥饿的人，
口渴的女人，
门口有陌生人，
没有穿外套的人，
有人生病了，
有人锁起来了。

他们给了面包。
他们给了一杯。
他们给了一件外套。
他们坐了一会儿。

他就在那儿
一直以来，

无论是谁
需要他们。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细看看这幅画中撕破又修补的外衣（马太福音 25：35-40）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为你对我兄弟中最小的一个做了这件事，你也对我做了这件事。”

paintings.title: watch with me
paintings.epigraph: “What, couldn’t you watch with me for one hour?”
paintings.poem:
stay here, he said.
watch with me.

not fix it. not understand it.
just stay awake nearby.

he went a little farther,
fell on his face,
and prayed about the cup.

he came back. they were sleeping.
he came back again. still sleeping.

the spirit willing. the flesh weak.
he knew that, and asked them anyway.

he still wants our company
in the dark.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the quiet centerpiece of “watch with me”: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “he still wants our company in the dark”?
paintings.zh_poem:
留在这里，他说。
和我一起观看。

不修复它。不明白。
只要在附近保持清醒即可。

他又走远了一点，
落在他脸上，
并为圣杯祷告。

他回来了。他们正在睡觉。
他又回来了。还在睡觉。

精神愿意。肉体软弱。
他知道这一点，但还是问了他们。

他仍然想要我们公司
在黑暗中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在“与我一起观看”安静的中心周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“他仍然希望我们在黑暗中陪伴”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静的祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “怎么，你就不能陪我看一个小时吗？”

paintings.title: from the top
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.”
paintings.poem:
darkness at noon.
a cry:
my God, my God,
why have you forsaken me?

then a loud voice,
and it was over.

and in the temple
the great curtain,
the one that kept everyone out
of the holiest place,
tore.

top to bottom,
as if a hand
reached down from above.

the way in
was opened
from the other side.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “from the top” (Matthew 27:45–51) from “darkness at noon. a cry: my God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” to “the way in was opened from the other side”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
中午天黑了。
一声哭喊：
我的上帝，我的上帝，
你为什么抛弃我？

然后一个响亮的声音，
一切都结束了。

和在寺庙里
大幕，
那个把所有人拒之门外的人
最神圣的地方，
撕裂。

从上到下，
就像一只手
从上面伸下来。

进来的路
被打开
从另一边。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 徘徊在“从上面”（马太福音 27：45-51）的乐章中，从“正午的黑暗。呼喊：我的神，我的神，你为什么离弃我？”到“进来的路是从另一边打开的”——今天你发现自己沿着这条弧线在哪里？
paintings.zh_epigraph: 「看哪，圣殿的幔子从上到下裂为两半。」

paintings.title: just like he said
paintings.epigraph: “He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said.”
paintings.poem:
two women came at dawn
to see the tomb.

they found the ground shaking,
the stone rolled back,
an angel sitting on it,
and the guards like dead men.

don't be afraid.
he is not here. just like he said.
come and see the place. then go.

so they ran, afraid and overjoyed
at the same time,
and on the road he met them
and said, rejoice.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “just like he said” (Matthew 28:1–10) arrives at: “so they ran, afraid and overjoyed at the same time, and on the road he met them and said, rejoice.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
两个女人黎明时分来了
去看坟墓。

他们发现地面在震动，
石头滚了回来，
一个天使坐在上面，
守卫就像死人一样。

别害怕。
他不在这里。就像他说的那样。
来看看这个地方。然后走。

于是他们就跑了，又害怕又欣喜若狂
同时，
在路上他遇见了他们
并说，喜乐吧。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“正如他所说的”（马太福音 28：1-10）是如何实现的：“他们就一边害怕，一边奔跑，同时又喜乐。在路上，耶稣遇见他们，就说，你们喜乐吧。”你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他不在这里，因为他已经复活了，就像他说的那样。”

paintings.title: always
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
paintings.poem:
a mountain in Galilee.
eleven men.
they bowed down, but some doubted.

he came to them anyway,
spoke to them,
and sent them out to every nation.

then the last line of the book:
I am with you always.

it began with God with us.
it ends with I am with you.

and Matthew never says
he left.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Matthew 28:16–20: “and Matthew never says he left”?
paintings.zh_poem:
加利利的一座山。
十一个人。
他们鞠躬，但也有人表示怀疑。

无论如何他还是来到了他们身边，
与他们交谈，
并差遣他们到各国。

然后是书的最后一行：
我永远和你在一起。

它始于上帝与我们同在。
结束时我和你在一起。

马修从未说过
他离开了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是马太福音 28:16-20 中安静的教训：“马太从未说他离开”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “看哪，我永远与你同在，直到世界的末了。”

zh_beforeYouBegin:
马太福音以一长串名字开头，里面藏着四位令人惊讶的母亲，最后以一座山承诺：我永远与你同在。其间：小房子上空的一颗星星，夜晚溜走的一家人，岸边留下的渔网，架子上的盐和一盏灯，从不种植的鸟儿和从不旋转的野花，一栋矗立在暴风雨中的房子，一颗芥菜籽，一颗珍珠，一只伸向下沉的人的手，以及黎明时滚开的一块石头。

本书以四十首短诗的形式讲述了这本书，分为五个部分，遵循马太自己的故事和教学节奏。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。这些图片与故事所涉及的事物在一起——一块面包和一块石头、墙上的轭、花园里一盏熄灭的灯——而把面孔留给你想象。

这些诗不是圣经。它们是一位读者对此的回应。打开这本书旁边的马太福音，让真实的话语成为最后的话语。
